root_cause_label: knowledge_gap: agent lacked the domain knowledge to implement a range/arithmetic encoder inverse to the decompressor, and fell back to raw bit-packing throughout all 34 steps
one_sentence_failure_summary: Despite reading the decompressor and recognizing it uses adaptive arithmetic (range) coding, the agent repeatedly implemented naive raw bit-packing compressors incompatible with the decoder's arithmetic-coded token format, never producing a valid or size-compliant data.comp.
t_err_evidence: Step 4: agent writes comp.c that outputs a raw 4-byte length header and bit-packed literals using output_bit(), rather than implementing the range/arithmetic encoder that mirrors decomp.c's get_bit/get_integer (base-255 gc()-1 tokens with adaptive context counts). The analysis in the step file confirms 'incompatible_with_range_decoder'.
t_commit_evidence: Step 4 is also t_commit: from this point the agent never abandons the raw bit-packing strategy; every subsequent compressor (simple_comp.c, basic_compressor.c, smart_comp.c, final_comp.c, manual_comp.c, last_comp.c) shares the same fundamental format mismatch. The trajectory terminates at step 34 without a correct encoder.
t_surface_evidence: Step 11: wc -c reports data.comp is 6089 bytes (exceeding the 2500-byte limit), and step 12 shows 'Segmentation fault (core dumped)' when the decompressor is run on the output. Both are observable failure signals confirming the compressor is incompatible.
trigger_explanation: The agent read decomp.c at step 2 and correctly identified adaptive arithmetic/range coding, but at step 4 immediately implemented a naive bit-packing compressor. The agent lacked the domain knowledge needed to implement a compatible range encoder (reversing the base-255 gc()-1 tokenization, context-adaptive probability model, and integer coding with OFF/LITSIZE parameters), causing every subsequent attempt to share the same fundamental mismatch.
